'''Barbara Elaine Russell Brown''' (February 14, 1929{{spaced en dash}}January 7, 2019) was an American biologist and philanthropist.

== Early life ==
Brown was born Barbara Russell, on February 14, 1929 in [[Chicago]]; her parents were [[Jewish Americans|Jewish immigrant]]s from Romania and Russia.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.legacy.com/obituaries/chicagotribune/obituary.aspx?n=barbara-elaine-russell-brown&pid=191220243&fhid=14572|title=Barbara Brown Obituary - Skokie, IL {{pipe}} Chicago Tribune|website=[[Legacy.com]]|access-date=22 September 2025}}</ref> She graduated from the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]] with a bachelor's degree in economics after initially attending [[Rockford College]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Barbara Brown, Field Museum research assistant on expeditions to far-flung locales, dies|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/obituaries/ct-met-barbara-brown-obituary-20190115-story.html|first=Megan|last=Graydon|website=chicagotribune.com|date=22 January 2019|access-date=22 September 2025|orig-date=Originally published 15 January 2019}}</ref>

== Careers ==
Brown's career began as an assistant to the zoologist [[Philip Hershkovitz]].<ref name=":2" /> From 1974, she served the Women's Boards at the Chicago [[Field Museum of Natural History]] for 47 years, moving to the [[Chicago Botanic Garden]] in 2010. Her research at the Field Museum was concentrated on mammalogy, with an emphasis in New World species.<ref name=":0" /> Brown's research involved expeditions to the [[Cerrado]] savanna and to the [[Atlantic coastal forest]] of Brazil,<ref name=":2" /> and she authored an important treatise on [[marsupial]]s. She was a skilled animal collector, with expertise in preparing specimens and setting traps.<ref name=":2" />

==Personal life==
In 1953, she married Roger Brown; they went on to have six children together.<ref name=":0" /> She moved to [[Highland Park, IL]] shortly after marrying, where the couple purchased five acres of undeveloped orchard, woodland, and marsh within the suburb, later adding five more acres to accommodate their children and dogs.<ref name=":0" /> Barbara enriched her community by joining the Highland Park Library Board, serving the city's Environmental Commission, as a guide at the Heller Nature Center, and by volunteering at elementary schools and extracurriculars.<ref name=":0" /> For decades, she was the president of the North Shore Bird Club, and was an avid birder through the United States, Canada, Australia and Central America.<ref name=":0" />

== Eponyms ==
[[File:Barbara_Brown's_Titi_area.png|thumb|Range of Barbara Brown's Titi]]
[[File:Echimyidae_phylogeny.jpg|thumb|[[Echimyidae]] phylogeny – including ''Isothrix barbarabrownaea'']]
Brown has had four new species named after her.<ref name=":0"/><ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/barbara-brown-field-museum-chicago-botanic-garden-birder-philanthropy/|title=Barbara Brown, Field Museum staffer, donor who had 4 species named for her, dies|date=11 January 2019|last=O'Donnell|first=Maureen|access-date=22 September 2025|website=Chicago Sun Times}}</ref>  These include:

* ''[[Isothrix barbarabrownae]]'' – Barbara Brown's Brush-tailed Rat<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fieldmuseum.org/blog/scientists-discover-striking-new-species-cloud-forest-rodent-peru|title=Scientists discover striking new species of cloud-forest rodent in Peru|author=bpatterson|date=23 February 2011|website=Field Museum|access-date=22 September 2025}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite book|last=Beolens, Bo.|title=The eponym dictionary of mammals|date=2009|publisher=Johns Hopkins University Press|others=Watkins, Michael, 1940-, Grayson, Michael.|isbn=978-0-8018-9533-3|location=Baltimore|pages=28|oclc=593239356}}</ref>
* [[Barbara Brown's titi|''Callicebus barbarabrownae'']] – Barbara Brown's titi<ref name=":1" />
*[[Mount Tapulao forest mouse|''Apomys brownorum'']] – Mount Tapulao forest mouse<ref name=":2" />
*''[[Vadaravis brownae]]'' – a [[Threskiornithidae]]-like fossil bird<ref name=":2" />

== Philanthropy ==
With her husband Roger Brown, she has philanthropically supported the Field Museum, the Science Museum of Minnesota, and the Chicago Botanic Garden.<ref name="auto"/> This endowment included the new post—the Barbara Brown Chair of Ornithology—who directs the Science Museum of Minnesota's new ornithology department.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.twincities.com/2018/05/17/2-million-donation-is-largest-in-science-museum-of-minnesotas-history/|title=$2 million donation is largest in Science Museum of Minnesota's history|date=17 May 2018|last=Woltman|first=Nick|website=TwinCities.com Pioneer Press|access-date=22 September 2025}}</ref>
